1800 GOT JUNK Pricing in Jacksonville: Cost Guide

If you’re staring at a pile of old furniture, broken appliances, or a mountain of yard waste in Jacksonville, you’re probably wondering how much it will cost to get rid of it. 1-800-GOT-JUNK? is one of the most popular junk‑removal services in the area, and while their pricing is transparent, there are a few variables that can affect your final bill. This guide breaks down the pricing structure, typical price ranges, and tips to keep your quote as accurate as possible.

How 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Determines Pricing

Volume‑Based Pricing

The core of the 1-800-GOT-JUNK? pricing model is based on the amount of space your junk occupies in their truck. The company uses a simple “truck‑size” system—usually a 12‑ft or 16‑ft truck—so you’re essentially paying for the volume you fill, not the weight. A typical residential job in Jacksonville might fill 1/2 to 3/4 of a truck, which translates into a flat fee that covers everything from loading to disposal.

Types of Items & Special Handling

Most household junk—couches, mattresses, old electronics, and yard waste—falls under the standard rate. However, certain items require special handling. Hazardous materials (like paint cans or batteries), large construction debris, or items that need recycling may incur additional fees. 1-800-GOT-JUNK? will flag these during the initial quote, so you won’t be surprised by hidden charges later.

Seasonal & Promotional Discounts

Because Jacksonville’s climate encourages spring cleaning and summer renovations, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? often rolls out seasonal promos. Look out for “Spring Clean” discounts, “Move‑Out” specials, or local coupons that can shave 10‑20% off the base price. Signing up for their email list or following the company on social media is a quick way to catch these deals.

Typical Price Ranges in Jacksonville

Below are the most common job types and the price brackets you’ll see in Jacksonville. Prices are estimates based on 2024 data and can vary slightly depending on location within the city and the exact volume of junk.

  • Small Apartment Clean‑Out (1‑2 rooms): $150 – $250
  • Medium Home Declutter (3‑4 rooms, some yard waste): $250 – $400
  • Large House or Estate (5+ rooms, multiple appliances): $400 – $650
  • Construction Debris (concrete, bricks, lumber): $500 – $800 (additional handling fees may apply)
  • Full‑Truck Load (max capacity, mixed items): $600 – $900

These figures include labor, loading, transport, and disposal. If you’re unsure which category fits your project, the safest bet is to request a free on‑site estimate.

Factors That Can Change Your Quote

Even with a clear pricing model, a few factors can bump the final amount up or down:

  • Accessibility: Tight hallways, stairs, or limited parking can increase labor time.
  • Item Condition: Extremely heavy or broken items may need extra equipment.
  • Location: Jobs in the outskirts of Jacksonville might incur a small travel surcharge.
  • Volume Accuracy: Over‑estimating the space you’ll fill can lead to a higher flat fee.
  • Special Disposal: Hazardous waste, electronics, or items requiring recycling may add $20‑$50 per item.

How to Get the Most Accurate Quote

Getting a spot‑on estimate from 1-800-GOT-JUNK? is easier than you think. Follow these steps to avoid surprises:

  1. Gather a rough inventory of the items you want removed. Take photos if you can.
  2. Measure large pieces (e.g., a sofa or a mattress) to gauge how much space they’ll take.
  3. Identify any special items (paint, batteries, large appliances) that might need extra handling.

  5. During the on‑site visit, walk the driver through the items and point out any access challenges.

By being prepared, you’ll help the crew give you a precise price, and you’ll know exactly what you’re paying for.

Yes. 1-800-GOT-JUNK? has a minimum fee—usually around $130—for very small jobs. This ensures the crew’s time and travel costs are covered.
